title: Roadmap meta-plan drafted as tracking-only doc
body: This plan documents the multi-version arc from capabilities/*.json manifest convention (ADR-001, already shipped) through CLI status (V0, lockable now), static dashboard Capability Center + MCP read-only projection (V1, future with trigger conditions), and guided setup runner (V2, future with trigger conditions). The plan stays status:draft as a tracking document — it is NOT intended to be locked or dispatched. Only child plans carry executable work. V0 child plan is `docs/plans/2026-05-22-002-feat-capability-status-v0/`.

title: V1 and V2 deliberately NOT in features.json
body: To avoid the orchestrator treating future milestones as dispatch targets, this roadmap plan deliberately has no features.json. V1 (dashboard Capability Center + MCP read-only) and V2 (guided setup runner) are documented in plan.md prose with explicit trigger conditions but are NOT scaffolded as features. When a trigger fires, a new child plan opens with its own features.json. This sidesteps the gap that DontPanic's plan schema doesn't have first-class roadmap/milestone/trigger_condition semantics — see D003.

title: Meta-planning is not first-class in DontPanic — convention used here, schema gap memo'd
body: DontPanic's plan schema does NOT yet support 'roadmap' as a plan_kind, 'milestone' as a feature flag, or 'trigger_condition' as a field. The ingredients exist (parent/child plans, dependencies, decisions.jsonl, status enum) but the discipline of 'this plan tracks an arc, V1/V2 are documented but not dispatchable' lives entirely in the operator's head. This plan uses that learned convention deliberately and consistently. A future plan (`feat-meta-planning-first-class-v0` or similar) should promote the convention to schema-level support once 2-3 roadmap-style plans have benefited from the pattern. Memo'd at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-bayesian-Documents-GitHub/memory/feedback_dontpanic_meta_planning_gap.md`.

title: V0 slicing: V0 + V0.5 merged into a single lockable child plan
body: Earlier iteration of this roadmap proposed five milestones (V0 / V0.5 / V1 / V1.5 / V2). Pre-lock critique flagged that V0.5 (CLI status) directly depends on V0's manifest loader + schema validation and they're sequential, not parallel. Similarly V1.5 (MCP read-only projection) is too small to be its own milestone — folds into V1 (dashboard Capability Center, which exposes the same status data, just via different surface). Final shape: three milestones (V0 / V1 / V2). V0 covers loader + schema 1.1 bump + probe binding + adapter binding + plan-lock sidecar + CLI status. V1 bundles dashboard + MCP read-only. V2 is guided setup runner.

title: V1 trigger conditions specified explicitly
body: V1 child plan opens when ANY of these is met: (a) operator has used `dontpanic capabilities status` (V0) for ≥2 weeks and reports a specific friction the CLI does not address; (b) a third capability beyond Firebase + Linear hits configuration friction that benefits from visual review; (c) static/core dashboard ships independently (Plan 2026-05-09-004 amendment splits static from Firebase realtime), creating the surface this can hook into. Without one of these, V1 remains documented future state, not dispatch target.

title: V2 trigger conditions specified explicitly
body: V2 child plan opens when ANY of these is met: (a) operator has used CLI status (V0) and dashboard Capability Center (V1) and explicitly reports 'the status view tells me what's wrong but I want it to fix what it can'; (b) two or more capabilities have ≥5 setup_steps[] each, making copy-paste setup error-prone enough to justify automation; (c) agent-handoff JSON (from V0 --format=json) is being consumed by an external agent that wants to delegate the automatable-step execution back to DontPanic. Without one of these, V2 remains documented future state, not dispatch target.

title: Final outcome / north star captured in plan.md
body: Plan.md now includes a 'Final Outcome (Once Fully Implemented)' section that describes the end-state across seven dimensions: (1) capability is a first-class concept; (2) one discoverable status surface, three projections (CLI/dashboard/MCP); (3) agents and humans share the same task model (automatable vs human-required); (4) secrets are never stored or displayed; (5) setup is guided, not improvised; (6) onboarding stays small; (7) plans declare their capability needs; (8) system improves itself via single source of truth. This anchors the iterative slicing work to a coherent product vision, preventing 'too tactical' (only fix today's Firebase blocker) and 'too architectural' (build the full framework before one slice validates the shape) failure modes.

title: V0 split into V0a (already shipped/in-flight) + V0b (this roadmap's lockable child)
body: Pre-lock substrate review surfaced that plan 2026-05-21-001-feat-capability-manifest-consumers-v0 is status:active and overlaps directly with this roadmap's originally-drafted V0 child plan (manifest loader F001 done, probe + adapter capability_id binding F002+F003 in-flight). Two active plans claiming the same loader/probe/adapter substrate would be exactly the orchestration ambiguity these plans are supposed to prevent. Rebase: V0a = 2026-05-21-001 (manifest consumer foundation, not under this roadmap's direct control but acknowledged as the foundation); V0b = 2026-05-22-002 (status surface — additive setup_steps[] schema field + CLI status + plan-lock advisory sidecar). V0b reduces from 4 features to 3; manifest-loader/probe-binding/adapter-binding work is declared as V0a dependency, not re-scoped. V0b F002 (CLI) degrades gracefully when V0a F002 not yet shipped; V0b F003 (sidecar) couples more strictly to V0a F003. Diagram + V0 milestone section updated accordingly. Roadmap dependencies array now includes 2026-05-21-001.

title: V1 trigger restructured as prerequisite AND demand-signal pair
body: Original V1 trigger conditions used 'ANY of these is met' across a mixed set including 'static/core dashboard ships independently'. That formulation treats a prerequisite (you need a dashboard to render in) as if it were demand (the operator wanted this). The two are different: prerequisite without demand = solution looking for a problem; demand without prerequisite = can't actually ship. Restructured to require BOTH: a prerequisite (static/core dashboard substrate exists) AND at least one demand signal (operator-reported friction the CLI doesn't address, OR third-capability friction explicitly benefiting from visual review, OR external workflow specifically needing MCP read-only projection). V2 trigger conditions kept as 'ANY' because V2 has no analogous infrastructure prerequisite — the demand signals stand alone.

title: North-star language softened: manifest reduces per-surface multiplier, not per-capability minimum
body: Original 'Final Outcome' section claimed adding a new capability means 'one JSON file + a small wrapper' and 'appears everywhere' without per-service product code. That overclaims: probe implementations and adapter bindings still require code in some cases (the firebase-dashboard adapter, the printing-press MCP binary work, the linear adapter). Corrected wording: the manifest convention reduces the per-surface multiplier (one capability declared = all manifest-aware surfaces gain awareness simultaneously) but does NOT eliminate the per-capability minimum (probes + adapters still need code where the capability is more than a notification sink). This preserves the architectural ambition while removing the unsupportable claim that motivates premature scope expansion.

title: Roadmap promoted to active tracking parent with V1/V2 child plans
body: The operator explicitly requested completing the roadmap tracking meta-plan by building out subplans and implementing with the orchestrator. This overrides the earlier wait-for-more-trigger posture for V1/V2 while preserving the child-plan boundaries. Parent status moves draft -> active as a tracking parent; code still ships only in child plans. V1 child plan opened at docs/plans/2026-05-22-003-feat-capability-center-v1/ for static dashboard Capability Center + MCP read-only projection. V2 child plan opened at docs/plans/2026-05-22-004-feat-capability-guided-setup-v2/ for guided setup runner, drafted now but sequenced after V1.

title: V1 implemented — static dashboard Capability Center + read-only MCP projection shipped via child plan 2026-05-22-003
body: Child plan 2026-05-22-003-feat-capability-center-v1 closed F001 and F002 as passes:true after operator review. F001 (commit 16adf94) ships the static dashboard `pages/capabilities/` module that reads `dashboard/state/capabilities-status.json`, renders per-capability cards (status badge, owner_boundary chips, configured/missing lists, automatable vs human-required next actions, pending probe advisories), and degrades to a useful empty state without Firebase, Firestore, or Cloud Functions. F002 (commit 7facb7f) ships the read-only MCP tool `capabilities.get_status` that returns the same JSON envelope as `dontpanic capabilities status --format=json`, supports optional `capability_id` and `profile` filtering, surfaces missing-secret names only (never values), and refuses mutation. Local verification: 116 MCP tests + 28 capabilities CLI tests + dashboard suite + plan validation + sanitization all green; per-feature close-out memos at evidence/closeout-memo-F001.md and evidence/closeout-memo-F002.md, V1 close-out at evidence/closeout-memo-V1.md. V2 (docs/plans/2026-05-22-004-feat-capability-guided-setup-v2/) remains the next executable child plan and is NOT silently folded into V1 — guided setup and mutating execution stay out of V1 scope. D005/D009 trigger semantics are satisfied: the static dashboard substrate prerequisite was met by the existing dashboard/ module and the operator override in D011 served as the demand signal, with V1 evidence now cited here rather than waiting for additional calendar time.

title: V2 implemented — guided setup runner (print-plan, governed execution, evidence) shipped via child plan 2026-05-22-004
body: Child plan 2026-05-22-004-feat-capability-guided-setup-v2 closed F001 (print-only planning surface) and F002 (governed --automate-safe --confirm runner with positive allowlist policy) as passes:true via operator_resolved; F003 (setup-run evidence + sanitization) is implemented and pending audit signoff (features.json passes:true flip occurs at operator close-out). F001 (commit ceb25bf chain) prints the manifest's ordered setup_steps[] with automatable/human-required labels, command templates, verify-probe chips, and never spawns a subprocess. F002 enforces a default-deny allowlist (heads: npm subcommands, dontpanic, echo/printf, true/false), refuses shell metacharacters, unsubstituted <PLACEHOLDER> tokens, env-prefix VAR=value syntax, and surfaces spawn failures as captured CommandResult(127) so the post-step status probe still runs. F003 (commit 5a8f3a1) adds capabilities_setup_evidence.py: every governed run writes a structured JSON record (capability_id, before/after status, attempted_steps with sanitized stdout/stderr tails, denied_steps, skipped_human_required, derived next_human_actions, declared_requires names-only) to $DONTPANIC_HOME/setup-runs/ by default, or to a plan-supplied --evidence-dir when invoked from a plan. The CLI has no --no-evidence bypass — every governed --automate-safe --confirm run persists evidence unconditionally (test_cli_has_no_no_evidence_bypass_for_governed_setup_runs). Secret values are scrubbed via a layered regex sweep that covers JWTs, Authorization/Bearer headers, underscore-prefixed tokens (sk_/pk_/ghp_/etc.), dash-prefixed tokens (sk-/sk-ant-/sk-proj-/xoxb-/etc.), AWS access keys (AKIA*), NAME=value env-prefix, and generic token=/api_key=/password= forms; the requires-block is reported as declared names only and values never leave the process. Acceptance covered by test_capabilities_setup_evidence_f003.py (25 tests). D005/D006 trigger semantics for V2 are satisfied: D011 served as the executable-now demand signal; setup_steps[] backfill on firebase-dashboard.json + linear.json (V0b) is the per-capability prerequisite; F002's governed runner is the agent-handoff substrate. Roadmap status remains active as a tracking parent — V0a, V0b, V1 are complete; V2 is in progress with F001 + F002 closed (passes:true via operator_resolved) and F003 implementation under audit. A subsequent D-entry will record V2 close-out once F003 ships features.json passes:true. The file-of-truth for delta is each child plan's features.json + evidence/. Codex auditor F003-i0 (medium, documentation) flagged the inconsistency against child features.json F003 passes:false. Wording above corrected so the parent matches the child's source of truth: V2 is in progress, not complete, until F003 is signed off by operator close-out.
